notes: B2, second pass 2026-08-30. 29 panels. The founder answered the pitch question, and his answer unified three separate features into one rule.
the_headline: This tab loses its main job. Its home screen's first list is 'Nobody has agreed terms yet' — a pool of agreements waiting to be spent on a campaign. That is exactly what set-first deletes. The tab keeps two jobs: finding people, and hearing from them.
the_biggest_find: BrandRequestComposerScreen ALREADY ASKS EVERYTHING the new flow needs — commission %, fee, post-by, where she works, and requirement-vs-preference, all marked negotiable. Its contents move into 'Her terms' in the set wizard. The screen itself survives for approaches outside any campaign. Its mirror on her side is CollabRequestDetailScreen, which shows Commission, Fee, Post by, Where you'd work.
cross_app_journey: Three steps drawn on both phones: (1) you publish and her whole deal arrives as ONE screen and ONE notification — today it is two screens on two days; (2) she counters the money and stays in the set; (3) she counters the date or mode, cannot stay, and you choose END IT or DEFER HER, with both endings said plainly to her.
she_is_warned_before_she_counters: Her counter screen shows the set's date and mode as fixed, with a line saying that asking for a different day means the brand must move her or end it. Changing the day is not a small edit.
she_is_not_asked_twice: When deferred she is told 'they kept your terms and are putting together a set for that week'. She does not re-confirm — they are the terms she asked for.
hardest_work_is_invisible: The negotiation screen looks almost identical and must be re-anchored underneath — from a standalone brand_collab_request to her row in a set. The `negotiations` table was built for exactly that shape (keyed on campaign_influencer_id) and has never been used, 0 rows.

release.deploy_class: deploy-inert — mockups and specification only, no code

one_rule.founder: "if brand agreed on pitches then all agreed pitches into whether existing campaign which match set parameters.....if not matched then create new one."
one_rule.the_rule: Whenever a creator's agreed terms need a home, look across ALL open campaigns for a set matching AIM + a date she accepts + SHOOT MODE. Found, she joins it. Not found, a new set is built from what she agreed.
three_entry_points: she countered the date or mode and you deferred her
she pitched you and you accepted
you asked her outside a campaign and she agreed
one_rule.why_it_matters: Three features become one mechanic, and one pool. A creator who pitched and a creator who was asked can end up in the same new set, because they want the same thing.

pitch_form_gap: ⚠️ A pitch carries goal, proposed_commission_pct, proposed_fee, proposed_deliverables and a posting WINDOW — and NO SHOOT MODE. Two of the three matching parameters exist; the third does not. Without it, accepting a pitch drops her into whatever set fits the dates, which could commit her to travelling to a store she never agreed to visit. The fix is one field on the pitch form: store visit / remote / EITHER. "Either" is probably the common answer and makes matching easy. Pitches already in flight get asked once, when placed.
already_built_for_this: influencer_proposals.resulting_campaign_influencer_id already exists — a column built for exactly "which collaboration did this pitch become". Never used, 0 rows.
matching_shows_its_working: The where-she-lands screen lists the sets that do NOT fit, with the reason — "12 Sep, outside his window", "pay for content, he pitched for sale". Same discipline as the basket preview: a brand who cannot see why a set was excluded assumes the matching is broken.
